Nazarbayev University is a research university in Astana, the capital of Kazakhstan, founded in 2010 by President Nursultan Nazarbayev and named after him. It teaches in English, with many foreign professors, and has a special legal status that frees it from the usual Kazakh university rules.

It was built as the flagship of Kazakhstan's plan to turn oil wealth into a new class of scientists, engineers, doctors and managers, and to keep its best students at home; until then the state had sent many abroad on Bolashak scholarships. Partner universities in Britain and the United States helped set up its schools of engineering, medicine, business, education and others.

It stands on a large modern campus in the new capital (Astana became the capital in 1997). Its scale and spending are unusual for Central Asia. It reflects Kazakhstan's turn toward English, alongside Kazakh and Russian, after independence, part of the same bid for a place in the world as the Asian Winter Games of 2011.
